precepts.text: When she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes ye go a whoring.
precepts.point: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood with censers in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth. What do you do in the dark? Your secret sins.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
When Ezekiel dug in the wall, he saw “every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, or Guadalupe on the walls, today. Ezekiel 23 shows what they were putting on the walls: images of the gods of their enemies.

“Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea”. Israel looked at the pictures of her enemies on the wall, dressed up like princes.

“And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” As soon as she saw them, she wanted them. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes you will go a whoring.

So the imagery on the walls of the temple in Ezekiel 8 was not harmless decoration. The images of other nations and their gods drew Israel's eyes, and her eyes drew her heart after them. It is the same today with the images hung on our walls, and it is why the Lord said, I cannot be around you all, and went far off from his sanctuary.

precepts.text: This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
precepts.point: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood with censers in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth. What do you do in the dark? Your secret sins.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.

precepts.text: The women sat weeping for Tammuz at the door of the Lord's house: the mourning that followed the sacrifice of their own babies.
precepts.point: Manasseh made Judah err and do worse than the heathen the Lord had destroyed before them, the nations Joshua and the elders were sent to kill out of the land for the very same works.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh “caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom”. That valley, Gehenna, was where Israel burned its garbage, our refuse; the Muslims call it Gehenna, their hell. Where garbage used to be burned, they burned their children, in honor of Baal.

There was an order to it. In the spring they held orgies in honor of Ashtoreth, the fertility goddess, a black Hamite deity whose star is Venus and whose nose is knocked off the statues. Everyone slept with everyone, and the women got pregnant. Nine months later, in the winter, came the bull god, Baal, the sun god the Egyptians called Apis. The babies were laid on the plates of the brass bull with a fire under it and around it; as they burned they wiggled off into the flame, and drums were beaten to drown out their screams. That is what Manasseh was doing, by the thousands. Carnival babies, Freaknik and the club today are the same worship of that goddess.

Why sacrifice the babies? Ashtoreth gave birth to a baby god, Tammuz, and Tammuz died as an infant. The same way she lost her child, the women had to lose theirs, and the same way she wept for her child, they had to weep for the children they sacrificed on the altar. That is why Jesus is always pictured as a baby with Mary.

Ezekiel saw it: “Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” That is what they had to do once they were in that idolatry: weep for the babies they themselves had sacrificed. And it was worse than what is brought out here.

precepts.text: The prophet dug in the wall and found a hidden door leading to a chamber of secret idolatry.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
“Son of man, dig now in the wall: and when I had digged in the wall, behold a door.” The Lord had the prophet dig through a wall, and there was a hidden door leading to a chamber of secret idolatry.

That is what a secret place is: something hidden behind the wall, that has to be dug into to be found. It is the opposite of cherubims graved openly on the walls of the house of the Lord.

precepts.text: The ancients of Israel did their idolatry in the dark chambers of their imagery, saying the Lord seeth them not.
precepts.point: He made the most holy house twenty cubits long and twenty broad, overlaid with fine gold to the amount of six hundred talents, and the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers also with gold.
precepts.why:
Behind that hidden door the Lord showed the prophet “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.”

That is the abomination: worshipping images in secret, in the dark, thinking the Lord does not see. It is not the goodly images made openly for the house of the Lord. The ancients of Israel hid their idols in chambers; Solomon graved his cherubims on the walls for everyone to see, and did not bow to them.

precepts.why:
The son of Semiramis, the one she got all her glory from, is named only once in the Bible: Tammuz, the son of Nimrod and Semiramis. “Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” Israelite women were weeping for Tammuz. To lament means to weep for, to cry for.

This is why, in many of these Christian holidays, especially among the Catholics, you have many of our brothers and sisters weeping for the baby Jesus. They have these customs, the lighting of candles for the holy child, and it stems way back to ancient Babylon. That one lamented, adored as a little child in his mother’s arms, is the same as the mother and child of the Egyptians, the Mary and baby Jesus y’all be seeing. It’s just the same thing.

points: that the hand of the Lord God fell there upon me: Right? So Ezekiel being in captivity under Babylon, the Lord was dealing with him, and the Lord wanted to reveal to Ezekiel a lot of things, so he can know what's going on back at his land in Jerusalem.
Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: So remember Psalms 104:3-4: makes his spirits a flaming fire. Ministers of flaming fire.
And he put forth the form of an hand: So this angel put forth the form of a hand.
and took me by a lock of mine head: And took me by what? By the lock of mine head. So Ezekiel having locks, the only negroes can have. Right.
and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven: And that angel, which is that spirit, lifted him up between the earth, which is the ground, and the heavens, which is that firmament.

where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy: Now, watch this as he goes to the temple. Watch what the angel is going to reveal to Ezekiel of what's happening inside this temple in Jerusalem.

even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here: So what did they do? It's called an image of jealousy because why? They had other idols that they would put inside our temple that they would give homage to, replacing God with those images, false images.

but turn thee yet again, and thou shalt see greater abominations: And besides that, there's going to be worse things that the children of Israel are doing, besides the image of jealousy that they use to provoke God to jealousy.
behold every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts: So every abominable beast and creeping things, they had images of it.

And there stood before them seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel: You had elders of our people in Jerusalem, and they in secret chambers giving homage and reverence to all these different idols of creeping things and so forth. These were the elders of the people, who supposed to guide us in the understanding of how to serve God.
with every man his censer in his hand; and a thick cloud of incense went up: So they had incense in their hand.

every man in the chambers of his imagery: Every man in his chambers of his imagery. Whatever god they had in their mind that they wanted to give power to and worship, they would have the incense and they would give homage to that god. This is what the angel was revealing to Ezekiel.

The picture of Nimrod shows a branch in his left hand. “Then he said unto me, Hast thou seen this, O son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? for they have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose.”

When it says they put the branch to their nose, it comes from the worship of Nimrod. They had a branch that they would smell; I don’t want to say it was weed, but it had an aroma to it, and it all symbolized the worship of Nimrod. It was a pagan custom of the past.

note.label: | SABBATH EVENING CLASS: The Third Kingdom of Babylon

points: “As I sat in mine house, and the elders of Judah sat before me”. The elders of Judah in captivity came and sat down in front of Ezekiel, as if they were so righteous and had done nothing wrong.

The Lord “put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem”, where was “the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.”

“Seest thou what they do? even the great abominations that the house of Israel committeth here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary?” He dug through the hole in the wall, and “Go in, and behold the wicked abominations that they do here.” The Lord was about to show Ezekiel what these men sitting before him had been doing.

“Every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” All kinds of idols were painted inside the temple, with sodomite houses right next door. Seventy of the ancients of Israel stood before them with censers, and Jaazaniah in the midst.

“Hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” That is what a lot of brothers and some sisters believe today: that he isn’t watching.

“There sat women weeping for Tammuz.” Tammuz was the son of Semiramis, the reincarnation of Nimrod. That history carried all the way down, and today they call him baby Jesus: Tammuz died as a child and they worship him in child form. Roman Catholicism made Jesus the forever baby, always in Mary’s arms. The women say, this is just for the children; no, it is not.

In the inner court, between the porch and the altar, “about five and twenty men, with their backs toward the temple of the Lord, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east.” They were not praying toward the temple; they turned their backs to it. Be careful, you face-the-east brothers: that is what they were doing here.

“They have filled the land with violence, and have returned to provoke me to anger: and, lo, they put the branch to their nose.” They would light the branch and get high from it, like the weed people smoke today to feel good and tingly. God was angry with them then, and he is angry with you today. Those who say the weed opens visions to them are seeing the devil; they are opening portals to Satan.

“Therefore will I also deal in fury: mine eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: and though they cry in mine ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them.” God told Ezekiel he would kill these people for being so wicked while sitting before him as if they were righteous.
